Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-24 16:00 UTC
Duration: 68 minutes (recording)
Location: Zoom
Recording: https://redwood-recordings.internal/ff/ff-20251024-7b3d

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (Redwood, AE)
- Samir Patel (Redwood, SE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): quick pairing, auth + env focus, request for SOC2 & pricing, plan for benchmark

-- Transcript --
[00:00:05] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood infra team, and with me is Samir our solutions engineer. 
[00:01:10] Alex Rivera: Hey Maya, thanks. We're excited — we want a hands-on walk through the SDK. We have a small TypeScript service and a Python worker for async stuff.
[00:02:22] Samir Patel: Great, we'll do a live pairing. Plan is: quick auth patterns (.env, CI secrets, SSO), a typescript quickstart, then the Python worker, show the Console sandbox and Optimize hints, then talk about capacity options. Sound ok?
[00:03:45] Priya Nair: Yes, and we have security folks asking about KMS, audit logs, and data residency. Also need to know if we can rotate keys with our vault.
[00:04:30] Maya Chen: Totally. Redwood integrates with KMS and HSMs via the Private deployment, and hosted has envelope encryption with customer KMS where required. We'll send the SOC2 package and network diagram after.
[00:05:12] Tom Huang: Quick question up front — latency goal is 150ms tail at 512 tokens for our checkout completions. Is that realistic on hosted?
[00:06:03] Samir Patel: Short answer: maybe. Depends on model choice, batching, and whether you use dedicated pools. Hosted can hit low hundreds for smaller models, but for consistent 150ms tail you'd likely look at Dedicated or a private pool in-region. Quantization and kernel selection help too.
[00:07:20] Alex Rivera: Ok that helps. Walk us through the TypeScript quickstart, with auth.
[00:08:01] Samir Patel: Sure. On your dev machine you do npm i @redwood/inference (note: pacakge name in repo is redwood-inference, transcription sometimes flips). Then create .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx for quick local dev. Example:
[00:08:45] Samir Patel: (typing) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_test123
[00:09:12] Maya Chen: For CI we recommend not storing plaintext - put the key in your CI secrets and inject into the build. For cloud CI you can also use Vault or Secrets Manager. We also support short-lived tokens via SSO/OIDC if you want identity-bound credentials.
[00:10:05] Priya Nair: Does Redwood support SAML SSO? Our platform team uses Okta and requires RBAC.
[00:10:45] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML/SAML2 and OIDC are supported for the Console and you can map groups to RBAC roles. There was a small doc we can share — will attach in the follow-up.
[00:12:30] Samir Patel: Back to code — here's a minimal TS example: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small-v1', input: '...' }); (paraphrased)
[00:13:10] Alex Rivera: The package names are slightly different than our internal docs, can you send the exact package and version?
[00:13:35] Maya Chen: Yup, we'll send the fastpath-quickstart repo link. It has both node and python folders, sample .env.example, and a README.
[00:15:00] Samir Patel: Now Python quickstart: pip install redwood-inference-client, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your .env or export, then from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); resp = client.chat.create(...).
[00:16:20] Priya Nair: Does the Python client support streaming? Our worker uses streaming to pipe partial tokens to the UI.
[00:17:02] Samir Patel: Yes — both clients support server-sent events style streaming and websocket options. Small note: streaming with large batch windows can increase tail latencies depending on your pipeline.
[00:18:10] Alex Rivera: On keys and rotation — can we rotate keys without downtime?
[00:18:50] Maya Chen: You can create multiple API keys and do a rolling rotate. For CI we recommend using short-lived keys from OIDC or Vault to avoid long-lived secrets.
[00:20:05] Tom Huang: We may need on-prem for PCI data residency. What's the path for Private deployment?
[00:21:00] Samir Patel: Private has two flavors: VPC-hosted private control plane in your cloud account, or fully on-prem with our package. Both integrate with your KMS and support audit logs. For PCI you probably want the private package and we'll coordinate an offline review with security.
[00:22:30] Priya Nair: Any changes in the SDK for private deployments?
[00:23:05] Samir Patel: No code changes — same SDK endpoints but you'll point to your private control plane URL and use customer-managed tokens. We try to keep the API/SDK surface identical across hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:24:40] Alex Rivera: Can you show the Console quickly? Where do we see token cost and latency?
[00:25:15] Maya Chen: (screen share) Console -> Projects -> Routes. Each route shows per-token breakdown, median and p95 latency, and Optimize suggestions like batch window tuning and quantization profile recommendations.
[00:26:50] Samir Patel: Optimize will suggest e.g., reduce batch window from 50ms to 20ms for lower latency at cost of throughput — it's workload dependent. We'll demo a sample job later in the benchmark.
[00:28:10] Alex Rivera: About billing — do you have predictable unit economics for embeddings vs generation? Our legal asks for a baseline forecast.
[00:28:50] Maya Chen: Yes, hosted is usage based (per-token), Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and lower per-token price. We'll include a sample TCO calc in the follow-up.
[00:30:00] Priya Nair: Any gotchas for local dev (Docker) and .env? We tend to commit env.example but never real keys.
[00:30:40] Samir Patel: Right, commit .env.example, never commit real keys. For Docker, pass secrets via --env-file at runtime or use your CI to inject at build time. Also, we recommend prefixing env vars with REDWOOD_ to avoid collisions.
[00:32:12] Alex Rivera: On caching — we use prefix caching for repeated prompts. Does Redwood do prefix/KV cache?
[00:33:00] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood runtime supports KV/prefix caching and will reuse cached KV for repeated context. You'll see cost improvements; sometimes transcription shows it as K-V cash, heh.
[00:34:20] Tom Huang: What about canary rollouts for model changes?
[00:35:05] Maya Chen: Console supports canary deploys and A/B with traffic split. You can pin model versions and route e.g., 10% traffic to new variant. Also automatic fallback policies if latency spikes.
[00:36:30] Priya Nair: Security specifics — where do we get the SOC2 and pen-test reports?
[00:37:10] Maya Chen: We'll attach the SOC2 report and a network diagram in the follow-up to the email. If you need an NDAed package we can coordinate through sales ops.
[00:38:50] Alex Rivera: For the benchmark slot — we prefer dedicated in our preferred region. How long would Redwood need to run a proper latency/cost benchmark?
[00:39:30] Samir Patel: Minimum 2 weeks to capture steady state and peak windows. For head-to-head we'd do a pre-run with a small sample and then a full-run with your traffic shape.
[00:41:10] Tom Huang: Are there managed metrics we can feed into our observability stack?
[00:41:50] Maya Chen: Yes, export via tracing hooks or webhook events; logs and traces can be shipped to DataDog/Prometheus/our Console. We'll share the tracing hooks doc.
[00:43:00] Priya Nair: Any limitations on embedding sizes or concurrent calls that we should know?
[00:43:45] Samir Patel: Embedding limits depend on model; concurrent calls depend on capacity. We'll map your concurrency profile in the sizing exercise.
[00:45:20] Alex Rivera: Ok let's do a short live run — Samir, can you call the sample TypeScript route and show a request/response?
[00:46:00] Samir Patel: (running) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-small-v1","input":"Create a checkout summary..."}'
[00:46:50] (brief pause)
[00:47:15] Samir Patel: Response stream shows partial tokens, you can pipe into UI. Note the p95 here is about 220ms in sandbox with small model.
[00:48:40] Alex Rivera: Sandbox numbers look promising. Quick question: how do we test the dedicated pool? Is there a demo endpoint?
[00:49:10] Maya Chen: We can provision a temporary dedicated pool for benchmark weeks. It will be in your region. We'll propose specs in the Sizing doc.
[00:50:55] Priya Nair: Any specific firewall rules for VPC peering?
[00:51:30] Samir Patel: We'll provide an allowlist and a diagram — typically egress to our control plane on specific ports, and optional private link configuration for full isolation.
[00:52:50] Tom Huang: One more — what happens on model degradation, how do you detect regressions?
[00:53:25] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets. If a regression triggers, you can alert and automatically fallback to previous model version. Also supports manual rollback.
[00:55:00] Alex Rivera: Good. Any concerns on data retention for PCI?
[00:55:40] Maya Chen: For Private deployments we can set retention windows; hosted offers configurable retention and enterprise agreements for stricter retention. We'll include retention SLAs in the doc.
[00:57:10] Priya Nair: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[00:57:30] Maya Chen: Recap — Maya will share fastpath-quickstart repo, SOC2 + network diagram; Samir will run a sizing/pricing doc and propose benchmark window; Priya will send traffic profile and latency SLOs. We'll schedule benchmark week of 11/3.
[00:58:10] Tom Huang: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[00:58:40] Alex Rivera: No blockers from dev team.
[00:59:15] Samir Patel: I'll follow up with an email with attachments and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[01:00:30] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we appreciate the time. We'll be in touch.
[01:01:05] (meeting closes, brief small talk)

End of transcript.
